newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares weak at lunch, seeking direction.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares weak at lunch, seeking direction.

text.p: Singapore shares were weaker at Wednesday's midday break with no immediate sign of an upturn as dealers contemplated the market's next likely landing point.
"The market is in contemplative mood at the moment deciding on which way to go," one dealer at a local firm said.
"At the moment we're heading down and are drifting there all the way," he added.
At the 0430 GMT lunchtime break, the Straits Times Industrials Index was sagging, down 22.42 at 2,090.55.
Low volume of 57.1 million shares gave reassured dealers that a major sell down did not appear to be in progress.
"This is not dedicated selling," said one.
But the downward drift saw 251 counters lose ground against 55 stocks that gained in the morning session.
Osprey Maritime was one gainer, up 14 cents at Singapore $2.30 after news of its US$750 million takeover of UK-owned Gotaas-Larsen.
Singapore Press foreign shares led risers, up S$0.50 at S$29.60. Creative Technology lead the losers for the second day on profit taking, down S$2.00 to S$24.90.
Top active share was recent listing Popular Holdings, down S$0.005 at S$0.495. -- Singapore newsroom (65 8703011)
